title: Chicken Balti Pie
subtitle: A British curry-house pie with spiced chicken thigh filling
excerpt: A shortcrust pie filled with tender chicken thighs in a balti-spiced tomato sauce. Born in British curry houses, eaten everywhere from football grounds to kitchen tables.
sourceNotes: British curry-house pie tradition, adapted for a standard 23cm shortcrust pie dish.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the filling only. Defrost fully, then assemble and bake fresh for the best pastry.
recipe.batchNotes: The filling doubles well and freezes in portions for future pies.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the filling up to 2 days ahead. Keep chilled and assemble on the day.

content.text: The chicken balti pie is a British institution, most famous at football grounds in the Midlands. The filling is a quick balti-style curry with chicken thigh, cooked down until thick enough to sit inside pastry without making the base soggy. Cool it properly before assembling.

items.prepNote: two thirds for the base, one third for the lid

content.text: Heat the oil in the frying pan over a medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 10 minutes until soft and golden. Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 2 minutes more.
Add the cumin, coriander, turmeric, chilli powder and half the garam masala. Stir and cook for 1 minute so the spices bloom.
Add the chicken chunks. Stir to coat in the spice mixture. Cook for 5 minutes until the chicken is sealed on all sides.

Add the tinned tomatoes. Stir well and bring to a simmer. Cook uncovered for 20 minutes until the sauce is thick. Stir in the remaining garam masala and the fresh coriander if using. Season with salt. Leave to cool completely.
Heat the oven to 200C. Roll out two thirds of the pastry and line the pie dish, leaving a little overhang.
Spoon the cold filling into the case. Roll the remaining pastry for a lid. Brush the rim with beaten egg and press the lid on firmly. Trim and crimp the edges.
Cut two slits in the top. Brush all over with beaten egg. Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the pastry is deep golden. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

items.symptom: The sauce is too thin and makes the base soggy.
items.cause: The curry was not reduced for long enough before assembling.
items.fix: The filling should be thick enough to hold its shape on a spoon. Simmer with the lid off until it reaches that consistency.

items.cause: The spices were added to a wet pan and did not cook in the oil.
items.fix: Make sure the onion mixture is fairly dry before adding the spices, and let them sizzle in the oil for a full minute before adding anything liquid.

items.symptom: The pastry lid slides off after baking.
items.cause: The rim was not brushed with egg before pressing the lid on.
items.fix: Brush the pastry rim generously with beaten egg before laying the lid on, then press firmly and crimp immediately.
